decision.explanation: The documents present two conflicting narratives regarding Donald Alexander Macdonald's career. Document 1 (D1S1-D1S16) explicitly states he served as 'Lieutenant Governor of Ontario' (1875-1880), 'Member of the Canadian House of Commons', and implies his role in the Liberal Party. Document 2 (D2S2-D2S16) claims he held the position of 'procurador en Cortes' (member of the Cortes Españolas) from 1943 to 1977, served as a 'Special envoy to Spain', and was a 'Member of the Legislative Assembly of the Province of Canada'. The prompt instructions require preserving all supported alternate referents and not silently equating competing assertions, even if they describe the same name with contradictory timelines/roles. Therefore, all positions explicitly mentioned in the source texts as held by Donald Alexander Macdonald are included. C6 ('Member of the Liberal Party of Canada') is excluded because the text describes him as a 'prominent figure in the Liberal Party' (D1S10), which denotes affiliation rather than a specific 'position' or 'office' held in the same grammatical sense as the other roles, though it is a valid attribute.
